user.description: Presence detection from Wi-Fi access point association tables. After this, add your access points and the devices to track from the integration page.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Already configured. Add access points and devices from the integration page.

menu_options.collect: Collect a report from an access point

data_description.consider_home: How long a device stays home after it was last seen associated to any access point. Covers roaming between access points, coverage gaps and a failing access point. Values under 30 s act as 30 s (away after one missed poll).

collect.title: Collect a report from an access point
collect.description: For an access point that isn't supported yet: Home Assistant logs in over SSH, runs commands that only display information (anything that could change settings is refused) and keeps a redacted report. Then download it with Download diagnostics on the integration page and attach it to a "New access point model" issue. The password is used for this login only and not stored.

data_description.profile: Generic tries common show/get commands. Choose a vendor list if yours is there.
data_description.commands: One per line: a command you know lists the connected clients. Commands that could change settings are refused.
data_description.legacy_ssh: Turn on if the connection fails with an algorithm error (older access points, e.g. D-Link DAP).

progress.collecting: Collecting a report from {host}. This takes up to a minute or two.

error.invalid_auth: The access point rejected the username or password.
error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the access point over SSH. Check the address, port and that SSH is enabled.
error.legacy_ssh: The access point only offers old SSH algorithms. Turn on "Allow old SSH algorithms" and try again.
error.timeout: The access point did not finish answering in time.
error.unknown: Unexpected error, see the Home Assistant log.

abort.report_ready: Report collected. Download it: on the integration page, open the menu (⋮) and choose Download diagnostics. Read it before sharing: automatic redaction can't recognise everything (a Wi-Fi passphrase, names, serial numbers). The report is kept until Home Assistant restarts or you collect another.

user.description: Choose how this access point is read.

details.description: Settings for {type}. They are tested by reading the access point's client list once.

data_description.name: Leave empty to use the name the access point reports about itself (for D-Link, its system name; for UniFi, its name in the UniFi Network application), or else its host.
data_description.ap_mac: A UniFi access point known to the UniFi Network integration. Clients are read from its controller through that integration; no extra login is needed.

reconfigure.description: Settings for {type}. Leave the password empty to keep the current one.

data_description.name: Leave empty to use the name the access point reports about itself (for D-Link, its system name; for UniFi, its name in the UniFi Network application), or else its host.
data_description.ap_mac: A UniFi access point known to the UniFi Network integration. Clients are read from its controller through that integration; no extra login is needed.

error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the access point or read its client list.
error.invalid_auth: The access point rejected the username or password.
error.unknown: Unexpected error while reading the access point. See the Home Assistant log for details.

abort.already_configured: This access point is already configured.
abort.unknown_driver: This access point uses a type that is no longer available. Remove it and add it again.
abort.no_unifi_access_points: No UniFi access points are available. Set up the UniFi Network integration first (with a site that has access points), or all of its access points are already added.

user.description: Choose a currently associated device or type its Wi-Fi MAC address. For phones with private Wi-Fi addresses, use the address shown in the phone's settings for your network.

reconfigure.description: Rename the device with MAC address {mac}.
